- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to account for potential rebound or volatility.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to premature declines after peaks.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment shifts — model reacts too slowly to sentiment changes.
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.6–0.8), model often underestimates upside potential; when falling, overestimates downside.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends into 30d horizon — history shows model overfits recent momentum, especially in 1–2 week windows.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high, model should not assume it will persist; if low, don’t assume it will stay low — adjust for volatility decay.
